summary.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning

details: Agent-learning environments are hand-built and static: they cannot target a specific policy's weaknesses and become uninformative as the policy improves.
Existing automated environment-generation pipelines are domain-specific and depend on LLM-generated (unreliable) verifiers.

EnvHarness: a domain-agnostic programmable layer that wraps a frozen environment purely through its standard reset/step interface, reshaping initial state (Stage), action/transition/observation maps (Contract), and composition of multiple environments into extended episodes (Chain), while the original tasks and human-built verifier stay untouched; components compose freely.

EnvRigger: an automated designer that treats the policy as a black box and closes an Observe -> Diagnose -> Write -> Validate loop, synthesizing EnvHarness components against diagnosed behavioral flaws and accepting them only if fresh policy rollouts show the reshaped environment is both challenging and solvable.
ALFWorld (embodied text), WebArena (web), SWE-bench Verified (software engineering), OfficeQA and SpreadsheetBench (office automation); WebShop added for RL analysis.
Native metrics per benchmark plus average steps per episode on SWE-bench Verified as an efficiency measure; disjoint train/eval splits, one attempt per eval instance.
Chain excluded from the automated EnvRigger pipeline (designer cannot observe internal states of joined environments) and analyzed separately.
Main setting: skill-based learning, where skills are distilled from rollout trajectories following ReasoningBank and given to the policy at eval time.
Policy and EnvRigger use the same backbone to rule out distillation from a stronger model: Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite (ALFWorld, WebArena), Gemini-3.5-Flash elsewhere.
RL setting: Qwen3-8B-base trained with GRPO on ALFWorld and WebShop, comparing original vs. EnvHarness environments as the training source.
No Skills (frozen policy), Original Envs (skills from unmodified environments), and domain-specific generators GenEnv (ALFWorld), VeriEnv, SWE-smith (SWE-bench).
All baselines share the same seed instances, environment count, skill-extraction pipeline, and policy model; no generation baseline exists for the office-automation domains.

Environment scaling: batches of 50 environments up to 300 under identical budget and retrieval protocol, comparing EnvHarness (co-evolving with the skill-equipped policy) vs. original vs. SWE-smith environments.
Cross-model transfer on SWE-bench with four policies (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Qwen3.6 27B, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6).

Chain-only vs. Stage/Contract-only vs. combined skills on long-horizon (paired) environments; user-specified constraints (quantitative success-rate/step targets and natural-language weakness descriptions).

key_findings.finding: Skills learned in EnvHarness-reshaped environments consistently beat those from the original static environments and from domain-specific environment generators.
key_findings.evidence: Up to +9.0 points on held-out ALFWorld instances over original environments; +5.7 average (and +8.5 OOD) over GenEnv on ALFWorld; +2.46 success-rate points over the purpose-built SWE-smith on SWE-bench Verified. Skills from unmodified environments can hurt: they fall below the no-skill baseline on SpreadsheetBench and lengthen SWE-bench trajectories.

key_findings.finding: Targeted reshaping also makes agents more efficient, not just more accurate.
key_findings.evidence: On SWE-bench Verified average steps per episode drop from 53.58 (no skills) to 49.61 with EnvHarness skills, while original-environment skills increase it to 55.01; EnvHarness also uses 5.11 fewer steps per episode than SWE-smith.

key_findings.finding: Policy-conditioned environment reshaping keeps scaling where unconditioned environment supply saturates, enabling policy-environment co-evolution.
key_findings.evidence: Under an identical budget of up to 300 SWE-bench environments, EnvHarness rises from 47.67 to 54.79 (+7.12) and is still improving, versus 52.13 for original and 50.37 for SWE-smith-generated environments.

key_findings.finding: EnvHarness environments provide a better optimization signal for online RL, not just for skill extraction.
key_findings.evidence: GRPO on Qwen3-8B-base: ALFWorld in-distribution success 87.9 vs 81.4 (average 88.4 vs 85.5) and WebShop score 79.2 vs 75.6 with success 67.4 vs 66.0; only ALFWorld OOD is marginally lower (88.8 vs 89.6).

key_findings.finding: Gains are robust across policy strength and model family, and the Chain component contributes a distinct, complementary long-horizon benefit.
key_findings.evidence: Across four policies with skill-free rates spanning 30.7-67.2, EnvHarness beats original-environment skills by 2.7-3.7 absolute points. Chain-only skills cut average steps to 41.96 with SR 49.63, while combining Chain with Stage/Contract skills gives the best overall trade-off (54.30 SR, 43.12 steps).
